SoH (State of Health) is shown when the car exposes a direct battery-health value, or as an estimate derived from vehicle telemetry when a direct value is unavailable. 100% means the pack is at factory capacity. The orange trend line is a least-squares linear fit across all your recorded trips.
Tip: BYD\'s warranty covers the battery to 70% SoH for 8 years / 250,000 km.

1. Create a free account at tailscale.com, if you don\'t have one.

2. In the admin console, open Settings → Keys and tap Generate auth key. Leave Ephemeral OFF — an ephemeral key makes the car disappear from your network whenever it sleeps, and its address would change every time.
3. Copy the key (it starts with tskey-auth-) and paste it below, then tap Connect. The car joins your network and keeps the same address from then on.
4. Install Tailscale on your phone or laptop and sign into the same account. Anything signed in can then reach the car — nothing else can.

Worth doing once, in the admin console: open Machines → your car → Disable key expiry, or it drops off your network in about six months and only a trip to the car can fix it. Three ways to share the diagnostics log, together with the background helper\'s own log when there is one. Telegram sends it in full to your bot (set one up under Settings → Connections → Telegram). Save copies it to Download/BydTripStats/ on the car. Email via QR code uploads the most recent part and shows a code you scan with your phone to email a link to it; the link expires after 24 hours.

The report captures raw values from every data source on your car's head unit — numeric values, strings, and arrays.

GPS latitude and longitude are NOT included.

Everything else is included: battery state, motor data, gear, speed, drive modes, climate state, charging state, PHEV-specific values, etc.

Nothing is sent automatically. "Email via QR code" uploads the report to a temporary public host (litterbox) and shows a link that auto-deletes after 24 hours; anyone with the link can read it until then. The other options keep the report on your device.

These are plain http:// addresses. To encrypt the Tailscale one, turn on \"Serve over HTTPS\" on the Tailscale card in Settings → Connections.

Let the Tailscale daemon terminate TLS for the web companion, using a real certificate for this car\'s Tailscale name. The address becomes https:// instead of http://, so browsers stop calling it insecure — and features they only allow on a secure page, like notifications and copy-to-clipboard, start working.

Needs MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates switched on for your tailnet — both are one-time toggles in the Tailscale admin console under DNS. Only the .ts.net address gets encrypted; the WiFi address stays http://.
Use it exactly as shown — no \":8888\" on the end. The encrypted address uses the standard HTTPS port; only the http:// addresses need a port.
The first load can take a few seconds while the certificate is issued.
How to turn this on for your network
1. On your phone or computer, open the Tailscale admin console and go to DNS — login.tailscale.com/admin/dns. Do this once; it applies to every device on your network, not just the car.
2. Check MagicDNS is on. Confusingly, it is ON when the button reads \"Disable MagicDNS…\" — that button would turn it off, so leave it alone. If instead you see \"Enable MagicDNS…\", click it.
3. Under HTTPS Certificates, click \"Enable HTTPS…\" and confirm. This is what lets your devices get real certificates.
4. Come back here and switch Serve over HTTPS on. Nothing needs restarting.
5. Open the https:// address shown here — exactly as shown, with no port on the end. The first load takes a few seconds while the certificate is issued, then it is instant.

Both settings are free and apply to your whole Tailscale network. Enabling HTTPS does not expose anything to the internet — the certificate simply proves the car is who it says it is, to devices already on your network.
This car is on your tailnet as %1$s. The address above works from any of your Tailscale devices, wherever you are — and so does ADB, at port 5555.

The companion is reachable on your home network only. To reach it from anywhere, join the car to your Tailscale network under Settings → Connections → Tailscale — you sign in by scanning a QR code with your phone, and nothing has to be installed on the head unit. With Tailscale on your phone too, the car keeps a fixed 100.x address that works over mobile data, including while parked, when WiFi is off. No ports are opened on your router.

Three things to set once, in the Tailscale admin console: turn OFF key expiry for the car (otherwise it drops off the tailnet after about six months and only a visit to the car can fix it), do NOT set an exit node on the car (that would push its ABRP, MQTT and Telegram traffic through someone else\'s internet connection), and do NOT enable Funnel (that would put this companion on the public internet behind nothing but its PIN).

On DiLink-5, the head unit powers itself down about ten minutes after you switch the car off, so remote access stops then and returns when the car next wakes. While the car is on it works normally, which is still useful for reaching the companion or ADB when you are away from your own WiFi.

On DiLink-5, publishing stops shortly after you switch the car off: the head unit powers itself down within about ten minutes, and nothing runs after that. Expect a gap in Home Assistant between parking and your next drive, rather than a parked car reporting in. Publishing resumes on its own when the car next wakes.

On DiLink-5, telemetry stops shortly after you switch the car off: the head unit powers itself down within about ten minutes, and nothing runs after that. Charging sessions while parked are therefore not sent live to ABRP — they are still recorded on the car and appear in the app. Sending resumes on its own when the car next wakes.

How long the trip stays open after the car turns off. If the car comes back on within this window the recording resumes seamlessly (same trip, a new segment appears along with the cumulative distance in parenthesis). Past the window the trip ends and the next drive starts a new one. Default is 3 minutes.

When the timeout is reached while the app is open on screen, show a prompt to keep the trip going (and its live range projection) instead of stopping it — handy when you park but stay with the car. If you don\'t have the app open, or you leave it, the trip still stops automatically as usual. A kept trip ends once you drive again, tap Stop, or after ~30 min parked.

Auto-discard trips shorter than this when they end (datapoints, segments and stats are removed too). Useful for filtering out moving the car a few meters in the driveway or very short distances. Set to 0 to disable.

Heads-up: discarded trips disappear from everything that reads the trip table — history list, weekly/monthly/yearly consumption charts, monthly distance and energy totals, seasonal analysis, and the SoH degradation series. A high threshold over a quiet day means no point will be plotted for that day. The chart already ignores trips under 0.5 km, so only thresholds above that change the chart further.
Choose which battery percentage reading to display on the dashboard.

On PHEVs the BMS SoC is usually not reported — use Panel if BMS shows 0.\nBMS is more accurate (float) than Panel (integer). Also, larger divergence from Panel is a great indication that it is time for either 100% charge or charging calibration
Notify me when the pack\'s cell voltage spread stays above the limit.

Spread = highest cell − lowest cell. A healthy pack stays under ~20 mV; a persistently high spread can flag a weak cell. Alerts are suppressed below 5% and above 95% SoC, where a wide spread is normal.
This is a BYD Trip Stats Pro feature. Unlock Pro to receive imbalance alerts.

Background activity when car is off
Controls whether the telemetry service keeps running after the car is parked.

Always On (recommended default): the telemetry service keeps running after you park, taking continuous 12V/SoC samples into battery history and capturing off-state (e.g. overnight) charging. Small additional load on top of BYD\'s own stock background drain.\n\nNote: most BYD units cut Wi-Fi ~15 min after the car is switched off. So while parked, ADB-over-Wi-Fi, the Web Companion (PWA) and MQTT to a broker on your home network stop until the car powers on. MQTT to an internet-reachable broker (e.g. HiveMQ Cloud) usually keeps publishing, because the car stays on mobile data. The \"Keep Wi-Fi alive when car is off\" option below can hold Wi-Fi open on supported units.

Minimal: service self-stops 5 min after the car turns off, then a 90-min alarm briefly wakes it for a charging snapshot. Lower drain, but off-state samples are sparse, ADB is not always on, the Web Companion (PWA) is only reachable during the brief wake blip, and MQTT is idle between blips. Off-state charging is caught within ~90 min, after which it publishes for the rest of the charge.

Deep Sleep: service self-stops 5 min after the car turns off with no further wakeups. Allows the car\'s ECUs to reach full deep sleep. The Web Companion (PWA) is unreachable and MQTT is silent the whole time the car is parked; off-state charging is not captured live — only reconstructed from the SoC delta when the car next turns on.

Minimal wake-alarm: never fired yet%1$s. If this stays \"never\" after the car has been parked a while, your head unit powers off fully at park — Minimal then behaves like Deep Sleep, so use Always On for parked data.
Keep Wi-Fi alive when car is off

Turns Wi-Fi back on after the car is switched off — the head unit drops it a few minutes later — so the Web Companion and other local (home-network) tools stay reachable. Only acts while the car is off, and backs off if the 12V battery or state of charge gets low. Draws a little extra power while the car is off.\n\nIf you also use Electro, Overdrive or any other app that keeps Wi-Fi alive, turn this on in only ONE of them and disable it in the others — two keepalives running together can fight each other and waste power.

While parked, publishing depends on the Background activity mode and your broker. In Always On the service keeps running, but most BYD units cut WiFi ~15 min after the car is off — so a broker on your home network stops receiving until the car powers on, while an internet-reachable broker (e.g. HiveMQ Cloud) usually keeps getting data over mobile data. Minimal publishes only during the ~90-min wake blips, and Deep Sleep not at all.

Do I need internet or mobile signal?

No for normal use. Trips, charging sessions, charts, and local history are recorded entirely on-device.\n\nInternet is only needed for optional features such as app update checks, opening web links, MQTT / ABRP integration and Telegram backups if you enable them.
What is BYD Trip Stats Pro and what does it include?

Pro is an optional one-time unlock for premium extras — a small thank-you that helps support development. It's €9.99, paid once, for the lifetime of one vehicle (no subscription). Everything that was free stays free; Pro only adds new features:

• Cards dashboard layout — a larger, fully customisable dashboard of big tiles you can drag-reorder, show or hide
• Neon theme — a pure-black, OLED-friendly look with glowing power digits
• Cell imbalance alert — get notified when the pack's cell-voltage spread stays above a limit
• Battery health report — export a printable PDF/HTML of your State of Health, decline rate and projected date to 80%%
• Dashboard screenshots — tap the BYD logo to save the current screen
• SD card backup — save the database to a BydTripStats folder on a removable SD card

Unlocking: the code is tied to your specific car. Open Settings → Pro, scan the QR code with your phone (or copy your Vehicle ID) to request a code, then paste it back in. It's verified entirely on-device — no account, no sign-in, nothing leaves your car.
Why is \'auto/unknown\' shown at driving / regen modes?

The app reads drive and regen modes directly from the car's instrument cluster, but the car only broadcasts a mode value when you actively change it — it does not report the current mode on startup.

Until you tap a mode on the car display, the app has no value to show and falls back to 'Auto' (regen) or 'Unknown' (drive). To fix this:

1. Cycle through each regen level on the car's touchscreen once
2. Cycle through each drive mode (Eco / Normal / Sport) once

The app will immediately pick up both values and start recording them with every trip data point. You only need to do this once.
No network connectivity means trip will be missing from the history?

No. Trip history is stored locally and does not depend on mobile signal or Wi-Fi.\n\nA trip may close a little later only if live telemetry itself stops for a while. In that case the watchdog closes the active trip after 3 minutes of telemetry silence, anchored to the last packet the app received.
The app stops working after a car restart

You need to exclude BYD Trip Stats from the autostart-killer:

1. Open the Disable Autostart app (native BYD app, usually near the file explorer)
2. Find BYD Trip Stats and toggle its entry OFF
3. Open the app and hold the volume button for ~10 seconds to restart the car UI
4. Reopen the app

Important: you must repeat this step after every app update, because the permission resets on reinstall.
How do I back up my trip data?

Several methods are available — all produce the same standard SQLite file:

Local (simplest): Settings → App → Backup & Restore → Backup Now.

SD card (Pro): Backup & Restore → Backup to SD card. Survives an app uninstall.

Telegram (recommended): Connect a bot under Settings → Connections → Telegram, then send manually or on a schedule.

ADB: adb shell run-as com.byd.tripstats cat files/db_backup/FILENAME.db > local.db
I reinstalled the app — can I recover my backups?

Yes. Telegram: reconnect your bot token, then Restore from Telegram → refresh icon rediscovers all backups automatically.\n\nLocal: The .db files in Download/BydTripStats/ survive a reinstall. Open Backup & Restore, tap the refresh icon under Local Restore and they reappear.
How does Telegram automatic backup work?

Enable the Auto-backup toggle and pick Daily, Weekly, or Monthly.

• The first automatic backup runs after one full interval
• If the car is off when due, it fires on next boot
• Failed attempts are retried with exponential backoff

To stop: tap Disconnect bot.
How do I restore a backup pushed from my PC via ADB?

1. adb push backup.db /sdcard/Download/BydTripStats/backup.db
2. Open the app → Backup & Restore → Local Restore
3. Tap the refresh icon — the pushed file appears
4. Tap Restore and confirm

To read live data from this car (battery, range, speed, tyres…), BYD Trip Stats needs to relax one system setting on the head unit (the hidden-API restriction), scoped to the BYD vehicle libraries.

This is a device-wide setting. It reverts on reboot and the app re-applies it only when needed. You can change this later in Settings.

Without it the app runs but shows no vehicle data.

The app also keeps ADB switched on at all times, and this part isn't optional. The car switches ADB off every time it shuts down; the app switches it back on as it starts, because that is what lets it start recording by itself when you start the car.
You make this change at your own risk. BYD Trip Stats is provided \"as is\", without warranty of any kind.
